chapter_title: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral (NCERT Standard Practice Set)

questions.question_text: Bases turn the color of red litmus paper to _____.
Which term is defined as: 'A substance with a sour taste that turns blue litmus paper red.'?

sections.section_name: Section B (Short Answer Questions - 3 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Why can turmeric paper NOT be used to differentiate an acidic solution from a neutral solution?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Turmeric paper remains yellow in both acidic and neutral solutions, changing color to red only in basic solutions.

questions.question_text: Describe the practical activity with aim: 'To classify household liquid samples as acidic, basic, or neutral using litmus indicators.'. Outline key steps and conclusion.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Steps: Place a drop of each liquid sample on separate strips of blue and red litmus paper using a clean dropper., Observe and record any immediate or gradual color changes., Categorize samples based on color response.
Conclusion: Litmus paper explicitly differentiates acidic (blue->red), basic (red->blue), and neutral (no change) media.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study - 5 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Describe the origin, preparation, and characteristic color shifts of litmus, turmeric, and red rose extract indicators across acidic, basic, and neutral media.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Litmus: Extracted from lichens; turns red in acids, blue in bases, remains unchanged in neutral media. 2. Turmeric: Ground from Curcuma longa rhizome; remains yellow in acids and neutral media, turns deep red in bases. 3. Red Rose Extract: Warm water extraction of petals; turns bright magenta/red in acids, green in bases, and maintains original hue in neutral media.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: While eating at a restaurant, a curry stain fell on Rahul's white shirt. When his mother rubbed soap on the stain at home, it turned reddish-brown. Later, when rinsed thoroughly with water, the yellow color partially returned.
Question: Why did the yellow curry stain turn reddish-brown when rubbed with soap?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Curry contains turmeric. Soap is basic, and turmeric turns red/reddish-brown in basic solutions.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study - 5 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Explain how you would identify three unlabelled test tubes containing dilute acid, dilute base, and distilled water using only turmeric paper.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Dip turmeric paper in all 3 test tubes; the one turning paper red is the Base. 2. Mix drops from the Base with the remaining two test tubes separately. 3. Test the mixtures with turmeric paper; the mixture that restores turmeric to yellow contains the Acid (neutralization), leaving the remaining tube as Distilled Water.

questions.question_text: Outline the procedure and observations for investigating Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral in the laboratory.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Procedure: Place a drop of each liquid sample on separate strips of blue and red litmus paper using a clean dropper., Observe and record any immediate or gradual color changes., Categorize samples based on color response.
Observations: Lemon juice and vinegar turn blue litmus red (Acidic). Soap and baking soda turn red litmus blue (Basic). Water produces no change on either paper (Neutral).
